title: GAIA: Glass-Aware I/O Middleware
evidence_span: Institutional abstract describes quartz-glass archival storage and three coordinated data-placement/scheduling strategies.
problem: Hybrid mechanical-optical glass storage has movement and depth-traversal costs that conventional I/O schedulers do not model.
method_or_artifact: Zigzag data placement, Z-axis-first placement and shortest-moving-time-first scheduling based on predicted movement time.
workload_or_benchmark: Trace-driven simulations with enterprise-scale workloads and varied glass sizes; trace identities and sizes unresolved.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Quartz-glass archival storage model; mechanical X/Y stage and optical Z focus; implementation and simulator details unresolved.
limits: The institutional page reports up to 82% read-latency reduction, but the number is withheld pending trace, glass-size and baseline conditions. This is archival glass storage, not glass packaging or fabricated-chip evidence. Author spellings differ between institutional metadata and program/author-lab listings; DOI/title match and source variants are retained.

title: Adder-DCIM: A Parallel Bit-Flexible Digital CIM Joint Model Compression Framework for AdderNet Inference
evidence_span: The PKU research report describes Adder-DCIM as jointly combining CIM-friendly model compression, synchronous parallel digital CIM, and bit-flexible minimum-selector circuitry for AdderNet inference; it reports 28 nm results including 134 TOPS/W peak INT8 efficiency, 6.49 TOPS/mm2 throughput density, and model-specific 255/243 TOPS/W values at 4.2/4.4 average bits.
problem: AdderNet inference still faces multiplication cost, fine-grained sparsity, and mixed-precision utilization constraints in digital compute-in-memory deployments.
method_or_artifact: Joint model compression and parallel bit-flexible digital CIM framework using synchronous parallel DCIM and minimum-selector circuitry for AdderNet.
workload_or_benchmark: AdderNet inference with ResNet20 and ResNet50 cases; average bit widths reported as 4.2 and 4.4, while dataset and reference accuracy are not established in the source.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: 28 nm process; source reports INT8 peak energy efficiency of 134 TOPS/W and throughput density of 6.49 TOPS/mm2, with voltage, frequency, power boundary, and measured-versus-modeled status unresolved.
baselines: Not named in the institutional report
metrics: 255 TOPS/W for ResNet20 at 4.2 average bits
243 TOPS/W for ResNet50 at 4.4 average bits
limits: Institutional report claims are not a manuscript or independent validation.
Voltage, frequency, operation-count convention, macro/full-system power boundary, named baselines, and measured-silicon details are unresolved.
Accuracy loss below 0.4% lacks dataset, reference accuracy, and percentage-point convention.
Do not substitute AdapCIM or SEGA-DCIM papers for this exact title; manuscript recovery remains required.
